content.value_statement: AI coding work can drift without clear operating rules. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance for safe edits and context review.
actual_capabilities: Routes principle questions to general, diff-aware editing, repository context, or VibeCoder guidance.
Recommends reading relevant files before making changes.
Promotes minimal diffs that preserve existing style and scope.
Provides repository context checklists for README, package files, plans, and agent guidance.
Gives simple next-step guidance for nontechnical VibeCoder users.
Warns against secrets, protected paths, direct production deploys, and destructive operations.
limitations: It does not implement code changes; another implementation skill is expected for execution.
Most source guidance is written in Japanese, with limited English labels.
Shell examples are illustrative and should be adapted to the active tool environment.
It cannot verify project safety without reading the current repository context.

use_cases.title: Keep AI edits small
use_cases.description: Use the diff-aware guidance before changing files in an existing codebase.

use_cases.title: Prepare repository context
use_cases.description: Use the context checklist to inspect project files before planning or review.

use_cases.title: Guide nontechnical builders
use_cases.description: Use plain-language prompts to decide the next step during an app build.

prompt_templates.title: Get basic guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the principles skill. Explain what I should do next in simple language.

prompt_templates.title: Review before editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diff-aware editing guidance before changing files. Identify the smallest safe change for my request.

prompt_templates.title: Build repository context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository context guidance. Summarize the project structure, workflow files, current branch, and important files.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a safe workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use all relevant principles. Create a safe task flow that respects scope, protected paths, secrets, and handoff requirements.

output_examples.input: I want to change an existing feature without breaking other code.
output_examples.output: The assistant first reads the target file, identifies the smallest change, keeps formatting stable, and checks the diff before reporting.

output_examples.input: I am not technical and do not know what to do next.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the current project state in simple words and gives a short list of next phrases to use.

output_examples.input: Start work in a repository I have not seen before.
output_examples.output: The assistant reviews README, planning files, agent guidance, git state, and key configuration before proposing work.

best_practices: Read the relevant principle document before applying its guidance.
Keep guidance separate from implementation unless the user requests action.
Treat secrets and protected paths as out of scope during context review.
anti_patterns: Using this skill to make code changes directly.
Reading .env, secrets, or unrelated private files during context review.
Replacing whole files when a small edit would solve the request.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for development principles, safe editing, repository context review, or VibeCoder guidance.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and routes tasks. Use an implementation skill for code changes.

faq.question: Can it read repository files?
faq.answer: It can guide read-only context review for common project files. It also warns not to read secrets.

faq.question: Why does it mention Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that need shared coding principles.

faq.question: Is the guidance technical?
faq.answer: Some guidance is for developers. The VibeCoder section explains next steps in simple language.

faq.question: What files should be avoided?
faq.answer: Avoid .env files, secrets directories, protected paths, and files unrelated to the user task.
